To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) three-dimensional field calculation can be carried out by solving numerically a boundary integral equation of first kind, (ii) a closed-form expression for the potential due to charge over rectangular surface is used in the solution, and (iii) the accuracy of the field values is affected by the geometrical attributes such the aspect ratio and the modeling of the anode wire.

(i) the boundary integral equation method is a powerful tool in the calculation of electrostatic field in the vicinity of the anode wire, (ii) the three-dimensional field configuration is sensitive to the geometrical parameters such as the aspect-ratio and the wire modeling, (iii) the thin-wire approximation may be used in the field calculations with reasonable accuracy if the number of surfaces in the polygon model is increased to 32 or higher, (iv) the boundary integral method is more accurate
the three-dimensional electrostatic fields can be simulated with high accuracy and the effect of several attributes of a wire chamber can be studied using a novel boundary integral equation approach.
